PullRequest.Title: api: Preserve snippet whitespace in returned code actions
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #325990

Code actions retrieved through `vscode.executeCodeActionProvider` now retain `SnippetTextEdit.keepWhitespace` when their workspace edits are applied. Previously, the command round trip dropped the flag, allowing the editor to reindent whitespace the provider had already prepared.

Copy the flag when converting a workspace edit back to the extension API and extend the existing snippet round-trip test with a whitespace assertion. No new test cases are added.

### Manual verification

Reproduced in Windows Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev: direct application preserved two spaces, while applying the command's returned edit expanded them to four. Verified the fix in a launched OSS window and repeated the check in a fresh instance after review; the returned edit now preserves the two spaces and snippet placeholder selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: An extension invokes vscode.executeCodeActionProvider, receives code actions containing snippet WorkspaceEdits, and may apply a returned edit.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing API command executes the provider and returns its DTO across the command/extension-host boundary; extHostApiCommands then synchronously converts each returned code action and each workspace edit before resolving the extension's command promise. If the extension later calls workspace.applyEdit, that is a separate existing IPC and apply path. The new keepWhitespace assignment is synchronous scalar work inside the already-required per-edit conversion and adds no wait or boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the code-action provider command and receive code-action/workspace-edit DTOs in the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command invocation per extension request; the response can contain multiple code actions and edits, but conversion remains one pass over those existing results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command/provider round trip returned the same workspace-edit DTO, including keepWhitespace, and ran the same linear conversion; the converter simply failed to copy that one field into SnippetTextEdit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider response must arrive before the command promise resolves; this boundary and its placement are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and send a WorkspaceEdit to the main thread when the extension explicitly applies the returned edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one IPC per workspace.applyEdit call, containing all edits; no per-edit IPC is created by this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Applying a returned edit already used one bulk-edit IPC with the whole DTO; the patch only preserves a primitive option during the earlier round trip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This later boundary must complete for application, but it is not invoked by WorkspaceEdit.to and is unchanged by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of returned code actions and total text edits. WorkspaceEdit.to already performs O(E) object conversion and grouping; the patch adds one primitive property read/write only for the snippet subset, with no extra collection, parsing, serialization pass, or retained object.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The command is promise-based and result conversion is synchronous after the response. The patch adds no task, Promise, loop, queue, or concurrency burst; optional application remains one bulk IPC.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache exists in this converter, and the patch changes no provider cache, key, coalescing, positive/negative result handling, or cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line and both production callers were traced, and the downstream bulk-apply path confirms no additional boundary or multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact edit counts vary by provider, but the incremental cost is a constant scalar assignment per snippet and does not materially affect the existing linear conversion even for large responses.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves metadata within existing objects and loops without changing allocation cardinality, IPC count, parsing, concurrency, or retained lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: An extension invokes vscode.executeDocumentRenameProvider and receives a WorkspaceEdit that may contain snippet edits.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing rename-provider command/IPC must complete, then WorkspaceEdit.to synchronously converts the returned edits before resolving. The added assignment occurs in the existing per-edit branch and does not add a boundary or additional traversal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the rename provider and return one workspace-edit DTO to the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider command boundary per rename request; all returned edits are carried together and converted once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider boundary and O(E) conversion occurred, but SnippetTextEdit.keepWhitespace was omitted from the reconstructed API object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing provider round trip is on the rename command's critical path; the patch does not introduce or move it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the reconstructed WorkspaceEdit as one bulk request if the extension applies it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per explicit apply call regardless of edit count; no new fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-request bulk application path existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for a subsequent apply action and unchanged by the converter patch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total edits in the rename WorkspaceEdit, with one pre-existing conversion iteration per edit and one additional scalar assignment per snippet edit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single asynchronous provider request followed by synchronous conversion; no new parallel work, limiter interaction, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing exists in WorkspaceEdit.to, and the diff does not alter rename-provider caching or reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: this is the converter's other production API-command caller, and its full before/after work differs only by the field copy.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Snippet edits in rename responses may be uncommon, but prevalence does not affect the conclusion because there is no scaling or boundary amplification mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Runtime cost and resource lifetime are materially unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. The sole runtime change copies an optional boolean during an existing O(E) WorkspaceEdit conversion; it adds no meaningful allocation, extra pass, boundary call, cache state, retained lifetime, scheduling change, or concurrency. No findings and no qualifying performance-regression fix were identified.
